atAGlance: Tender cubes of “shaking beef” seared in a hot wok, usually served with greens, tomato, onion, and a lime-pepper dipping salt.
whatItIs: Bò lúc lắc gets its name from the shaking motion of the pan. The beef is cut into cubes, quickly seared, and glossed with a fish-sauce-and-garlic glaze so the outside is browned while the inside stays juicy.
howToEnjoy: Dip a cube into lime, salt, and pepper before eating it with rice or salad. It is a good shared dish when you want something celebratory but easy to recognize.
howLocalsOrder: Bò lúc lắc is ordered for seared beef cubes, often with rice, salad, and lime-pepper salt. Ask for a fried egg or extra rice before the plate leaves the wok.
worthKnowing: The dish reflects Vietnam's restaurant-style comfort food: a little French steakhouse influence, a lot of wok heat, and the unmistakable Vietnamese habit of brightening rich meat with lime and herbs.
goodToKnow: The classic finishing move is dipping each beef cube into lime-pepper salt. It sharpens the buttery beef without turning the plate into a saucy stir-fry.
